$comment: The auth-callback contract: which redirect destinations exist, per surface, and how a mobile confirmation callback is parsed. TypeScript (tests/unit/auth-redirect-contract.test.ts), Swift (AuthCallbackTests) and Kotlin (AuthCallbackLinkTest) all read this file directly, so the three platforms cannot drift apart on what they accept. Redirects are never taken from a client request: each surface uses only its own destination below, and each Supabase project's allow-list carries exactly its own environment's rows.

faithform.$comment: One custom scheme for every build, by construction: iOS and Android both register `faithform` and neither declares Universal/App Links (a deliberate decision recorded in Info.plist and AndroidManifest.xml). Environment separation happens at the identity provider, not in the URL: each environment talks to its own Supabase project, the PKCE verifier is stored per environment, and a code minted by one project is meaningless to another.

confirmHandoff.$comment: The https page a confirmation email returns to, and the reason the apps no longer register the custom scheme itself as `redirect_to`. A custom scheme cannot be the final stop of a redirect chain: Supabase's verify endpoint confirms the address and then 302s to `redirect_to`, and browsers — the in-app browsers inside mail clients above all — refuse to follow a 302 into a non-http scheme. The address was already confirmed by then, so the person saw a connection error for an account that had in fact been created, and signing in worked. This page ends that: it receives the 302, hands the code on to `faithform.canonical` from a page it controls, and when the app does not open says so in words. It never exchanges the code — the PKCE verifier is in the phone's keychain — so it is a courier and nothing else. Staging's row is `{staging origin}/app/auth/callback`, uninvented here for the same reason the dashboard's is.

dashboard.$comment: The staging origin is a deployment decision this repository deliberately does not invent; its callback is <staging origin>/auth/callback.

vectors.$comment: accepted: exactly the mobile callback, carrying a code. failures: the mobile callback carrying a provider failure (or nothing) — parsed, shown as a typed state, never exchanged. rejected: not a mobile auth callback at all — including the dashboard callback, which must never be treated as one, and lookalikes a hostile link could carry. The parser returns nothing for these and the app does nothing.

accepted.why: scheme and host compare case-insensitively, as URLs do
extra parameters the provider appends are ignored, not fatal

failures.why: the provider reports failures in the fragment
and some versions report them in the query
a percent-encoded description must be parsed, not crash the parser: decoding it yields a space, which some URL APIs refuse as query input
the same shape a real provider sends, fully percent-encoded
a malformed percent escape is tolerated: the reason still reads, and nothing throws
our callback shape carrying neither a code nor an error is a broken link, shown as one
a code outside the contract bounds is refused before any network call
off-alphabet codes are refused before any network call

handoff.why: the ordinary success: the code travels on untouched
only the code is carried; parameters the provider appended are dropped rather than relayed
a failure reaches the app as a failure, so it shows the expired-link screen; the provider's wording is not relayed
a failure reported in the query is normalised into the fragment, which is where both parsers look first
an error code outside our own alphabet is dropped, not forwarded: nothing shapes the deep link but values this file names

handoffRefused.why: a code outside the contract bounds is never forwarded; the page explains instead
nothing to carry at all: the page says the address is confirmed and points at sign-in
a parameter that is neither a code nor an error carries no state to the app, and a destination is never taken from a link

rejected.why: a different faithform deep link is not an auth callback
a destination link is not an auth callback
the dashboard callback must never be consumed by the mobile app
the development dashboard callback must never be consumed by the mobile app

dashboardRejected.why: the mobile callback must never be accepted as a dashboard post-auth destination
absolute URLs are never accepted as a dashboard destination
